evidence.locator: text: Sections 2 and 4(a), 4(f), and Glossary definition of Modifications (reciprocal licensing and source duties attach to distributed modifications, defined as changes to a file containing Licensed Product or a new file containing any part of it; a Derivative Work may use another license if this license remains fulfilled for the Licensed Product and its modifications)

text: Sections 2 and 4(a), 4(b), and 4(f) (distributed file-level modifications remain governed by this license and their source must remain available, while larger Derivative Works may be distributed under another license), establishing file-scoped weak copyleft

text: Sections 4(a), 4(c)(i)-(ii), 4(d)-(e), and 5, plus Exhibit A (license copies in distributed modifications and relevant documentation, a source-file notice, conspicuous executable/documentation/collateral notice with source-location details, and conditional LEGAL-file disclosures create a material notice burden)

text: Sections 4(a)-(e) and 5 (distributed modifications must remain under this or a future version, carry the license and Exhibit A notice, and make source available without charge for as long as other forms are distributed; knowledge-based LEGAL-file updates, third-party notification, executable source-location notices, indemnity, and statutory-noncompliance descriptions have no complete vocabulary values and are represented by unknown); no network-use disclosure or installation-information duty is stated

text: Sections 1(b), 2(b), 3, and 9(b)-(c) (express royalty-free patent grants cover only claims necessary for covered Modifications or their Derivative Works, exclude deleted code and combinations, and grants from a Respondent terminate after the notice period for specified patent litigation unless withdrawn or licensed), supporting defensive-termination as the controlling classification

text: Sections 1(a)-(b), 2(a)-(b), and 4(e)-(g), read with the Preamble statements permitting any-purpose use and compensation in specified cases (use, reproduction, modification, distribution, sublicensing, patent rights, private use, and conditional commercial exploitation are express)

text: Sections 3, 4(a), 4(d)-(e), 4(g), 5, 7(c), and 8-10, and Section 13 (restrictions cover additional terms, trademarks, patent claims, warranty, and liability; fee/compensation limits, indemnities, special noncompliance and license-renaming rules, general breach termination, California governing law, prevailing-party costs, and other litigation terms are not losslessly represented and therefore require unknown)

metadata: id=BitTorrent-1.1, name='BitTorrent Open Source License v1.1', deprecated=false, osi=false, fsf=true, and comments note the upstream Exhibit A version-number defect; text: Sections 3-5, 7(c), 9, and 13 contain material fee, disclosure, indemnity, termination, governing-law, and litigation-cost conditions outside the guide vocabulary, so this non-OSI version is not a safe general recommendation

text: Sections 4(a)-(g), 5, and 9(a)-(b), with complete-text review (distribution activates same-license, source, license, notice, and executable duties; specified patent litigation activates defensive termination; knowledge, compensation, statutory impossibility, license modification, and uncured breach are additional trigger dimensions represented by unknown; private modification, linking, and network or external deployment alone are not stated triggers)
